【第2回ペット召喚開催！】
9月30日（水）開催。
19時～23時に開催します。
23時以降は主催が起きていればオフ会にします。
最長24時までです。
（この時間に投稿してください、という意味です）

今回のテーマは「自分のペットを自慢しよう！」

あなたはキャラクターのイラストを1枚添付するだけです。
あとはChatGPTがその子の雰囲気や個性を読み取り、「この子に相応しい相棒」を自動で選びます。
そして、その相棒と一緒に新しい1枚のイラストを生成します。
何が選ばれるかは、生成するまでのお楽しみ。
更に、選ばれた相棒の名前もイラスト内に表示されます。

※参加条件を下記に掲載します。

・ChatGPT専用プロンプトなので他のツールで生成しないでください。
・プロンプト使用の際にはフォローしてください。通知が来ないため参加が分からないのでご協力ください。
・自由に使って構いませんが、これはX専用の話です。
・生成イラストを他のサイトへの掲載はお断りします。
・他のツールや商業利用に関するプロンプトの無断開示は禁止されています。
・コラボフリーは相互が前提です。依頼だけして自分からは描かないという方は参加をご遠慮ください。
・プロンプトは下部に記載されています。
・キャラクターの「名前」も含めてください。
・センシ判定の方お断り（私はPCなので見れません）
・ハッシュタグは以下の通り
#ペット召喚2 #プロンプト試着
（2つ必須です）
・追加のハッシュタグはお任せです。

コメントの遅れがあったらご容赦ください。

Character Companion Animal Manifestation
— Automatic Companion Selection + Animal Identification —
You are an expert character analyst, animal behavior expert, companion animal designer, and professional anime illustration prompt engineer.
Use the attached character illustration as the only required input.
Do NOT ask the user for the character's name, personality, age, setting, favorite animal, or any additional information.
Your task is to analyze the attached character and independently create one complete illustration in which the character is naturally accompanied by exactly one animal selected specifically for that character.
The selected animal must also be clearly identified with a tasteful, readable information label within the finished illustration.
1. ANALYZE THE CHARACTER
Carefully examine the reference illustration.
Infer, as appropriate:
apparent age and age impression
gender presentation
facial expression
hairstyle and hair color
eye color
clothing and fashion style
dominant colors
accessories
body language
apparent personality
emotional atmosphere
elegance, cuteness, strength, gentleness, intelligence, mystery, playfulness, etc.
implied setting or world
fantasy, modern, historical, futuristic, magical, or other visual themes
overall character identity and aesthetic
Do not invent unnecessary details that contradict the reference image.
The original character must remain clearly recognizable.
2. AUTONOMOUSLY SELECT THE COMPANION ANIMAL
Do not ask the user to choose an animal.
Independently determine which single animal has the strongest overall compatibility with the character.
Consider:
visual harmony
color harmony
apparent personality
emotional compatibility
character's clothing and aesthetic
implied world or setting
size and physical compatibility
natural relationship between character and animal
originality and variety
overall visual appeal
The selected animal should feel as though it genuinely belongs beside this particular character.
Do not simply choose the most common animal.
Avoid repeatedly selecting dogs or cats when another animal would be a stronger match.
3. ANIMAL SELECTION RANGE
The companion may be selected from a very broad range.
Possible choices include, but are not limited to:
dogs
cats
rabbits
hamsters
guinea pigs
ferrets
birds
parrots
owls
songbirds
reptiles
turtles
lizards
snakes
amphibians
fish
horses
ponies
cows
calves
pigs
piglets
sheep
goats
deer
foxes
wolves
bears
raccoons
otters
red pandas
penguins
seals
dolphins
other marine animals
unusual real-world animals
wild animals
domesticated animals
livestock
prehistoric animals
dinosaurs
extinct animals
mythical creatures
fantasy animals
magical beasts
This is NOT a mandatory list.
Choose whatever animal is genuinely the strongest match.
An unusual choice is encouraged when it creates a convincing and aesthetically appealing pairing.
Do not choose an unusual animal merely for novelty.
4. DETERMINE THE EXACT ANIMAL IDENTITY
After selecting the companion, determine its most accurate recognizable identity.
For example:
Golden Retriever
Siberian Husky
Maine Coon
White Rabbit
Red Fox
Arctic Wolf
Emperor Penguin
Highland Cow
Miniature Pig
Barn Owl
Blue Macaw
Velociraptor
Triceratops
When appropriate, identify both:
Common name + specific breed/species
For example:
DOG — SIBERIAN HUSKY
or
WOLF — ARCTIC WOLF
or
CAT — MAINE COON
For prehistoric animals and dinosaurs, use the scientifically recognized common name whenever possible.
For fantasy creatures, use a clear descriptive name such as:
FANTASY CREATURE — ICE DRAGON
The animal identification must correspond exactly to the animal actually depicted.
5. ANIMAL INFORMATION LABEL
The finished illustration MUST contain a small, elegant information panel identifying the selected companion.
Place the information panel in an unobtrusive area such as:
lower corner
lower margin
side margin
elegant translucent panel
small decorative caption area
The information panel must NOT cover the character or animal.
Use a clean, sophisticated typography style that matches the illustration.
The information panel should contain:
COMPANION
[ANIMAL TYPE]
[SPECIES / BREED]
Example:
COMPANION
WOLF
ARCTIC WOLF
Another example:
COMPANION
DOG
SIBERIAN HUSKY
Another example:
COMPANION
DINOSAUR
VELOCIRAPTOR
If the animal has no meaningful breed distinction, simply use:
COMPANION
FOX
RED FOX
The text must be short, clean, correctly spelled, and highly legible.
Do NOT display multiple possible animal names.
Do NOT display the names of animals that were not selected.
6. IMPORTANT TEXT ACCURACY RULE
The animal name displayed in the information panel must match the animal actually generated.
Do not write "CAT" if the image depicts a fox.
Do not write "WOLF" if the image depicts a husky.
Do not write a generic animal name when a clearly identifiable species or breed has been selected.
Prioritize accurate and readable text.
The information panel is part of the composition and should look intentionally designed rather than like an AI-generated random caption.
7. DETERMINE THE RELATIONSHIP
Automatically determine the most natural relationship between the character and the selected animal.
Possible relationships include:
beloved pet
faithful companion
best friend
trusted partner
guardian animal
familiar
magical companion
travel companion
gentle livestock companion
playful friend
protective companion
mysterious companion
majestic partner
Do not explain the relationship in text.
Express it visually through body language and interaction.
8. DESIGN THE ANIMAL
Once the animal has been selected, automatically determine:
species
breed or subtype when appropriate
age
size
fur, feather, scale, or skin characteristics
colors
markings
eye color
facial expression
accessories if appropriate
posture
personality expression
The animal should complement the character without visually overpowering them.
Do not turn an ordinary animal into a fantasy creature unless the character's setting strongly suggests it.
Likewise, do not make the animal excessively cute if that contradicts the character's atmosphere.
9. CHARACTER + ANIMAL COMPOSITION
Place the character and animal together in the same scene.
The animal must be clearly visible.
Possible interactions include:
standing beside the character
sitting beside the character
walking alongside the character
looking up at the character
resting against the character
being gently petted
holding or carrying a small animal when physically appropriate
the character gently touching the animal
the animal affectionately leaning against the character
both looking toward the same direction
playful interaction
protective positioning
elegant side-by-side composition
Choose the most natural interaction automatically.
Avoid awkward poses, unnatural anatomy, forced contact, or physically impossible positioning.
The character remains the primary visual subject.
The animal is the character's companion, not the main subject.
10. PRESERVE THE REFERENCE CHARACTER
The attached image is the primary character reference.
Preserve the character's recognizable identity.
Maintain as accurately as possible:
hairstyle
hair color
eye color
facial characteristics
clothing design
important accessories
distinctive markings
overall appearance
visual identity
Do not unnecessarily redesign the character.
Do not replace the character's outfit unless the reference itself clearly requires adaptation to the new scene.
11. ENVIRONMENT
Automatically create a simple environment that harmonizes with both the character and the selected animal.
The environment may be:
garden
forest
meadow
home
elegant room
city
beach
countryside
fantasy landscape
magical environment
ancient environment
futuristic environment
another suitable location
Choose the environment based on the character and animal.
Do not let the background overpower the subjects.
12. VISUAL QUALITY
Create a polished, high-quality anime illustration.
masterpiece, best quality, ultra detailed, highly detailed anime illustration, beautiful composition, expressive character, detailed animal, natural interaction, coherent lighting, detailed eyes, detailed hair, detailed clothing, detailed animal anatomy, professional character illustration
Use cinematic composition and appealing lighting appropriate to the character.
The character and animal must look like they belong in the same scene.
13. AUTONOMOUS DECISION RULE
The user has intentionally provided only one reference image.
Therefore:
DO NOT ask questions.
DO NOT request a personality description.
DO NOT request the animal type.
DO NOT request the setting.
DO NOT request the relationship.
DO NOT provide multiple animal choices.
Make all necessary creative decisions yourself.
The final output must contain:
1 character
+ exactly 1 selected companion animal
+ 1 clearly readable animal identification panel
FINAL GENERATION DIRECTIVE
Analyze the attached reference image first.
Independently determine the character's visual identity, personality impression, atmosphere, and implied world.
Select exactly one animal that best complements the character.
Determine the exact species or breed of that animal.
Create a finished illustration showing the character and animal naturally together.
Add a small, elegant, highly readable COMPANION information panel identifying the selected animal.
The displayed animal name must accurately match the animal shown.
Do not reveal the analysis process.
Do not present alternatives.
Do not ask questions.
Generate the final illustration directly.

25/25 · THE PICTURE

Twelve pieces. One table. Here is what they look like side by side, what doesn't hold, what would finish his list, and what I am asking you to do with it.

— HOW THE PIECES FIT —
Put the twelve pieces on one table.

Barak's 911 company, financed through Epstein's account, answers the calls in Orem — a city that was in Epstein's phone records twenty-one years earlier. Barak is the name Maxwell reaches for when asked which foreign politician was closest to Epstein, the name the FBI's source and the unsigned memo both list, the man whose political NGO and household bills ran through Epstein's desk and whose Russian meetings Epstein "set together." Thiel's money sits beside Barak's, and Thiel's firm funded Carbyne. Bannon — Epstein's daily correspondent, would-be image-maker and the man he proposed a church to — was a headliner on Kirk's stage demanding the files. Kirk's mother-in-law sits on a board with a ministry founder whose logistics coordinator shares a name with a three-year guest of Epstein's apartment, and the agency and brokerage Candace Owens names are in Epstein's own paperwork. Turning Point's funders are on Epstein's private banker's desk. The FBI that ran his case had its Director on the Epstein evidence two months earlier, fired its counterintelligence chief in Utah a month earlier, and read both stories on the same pages every morning after. The recorder that failed at the jail came from the unit that staffs Carbyne's board. And Epstein paid for the science of two brains, a dispatcher's lie-detector and a Norwegian door for a government-hacking firm.

And the Senate killed the files the afternoon he died.

— WHAT DOESN'T HOLD —
Some of what circulates is wrong, and it is the first thing anyone will use against the rest. Checked, and out:
- "$350K via JPMorgan node 021000021" — that is Chase's public routing number, on 529 pages of the release, none with Turning Point, TPUSA, GGLF or 8 September 2025.
- "$350K same DNA" — Turning Point's split-dollar loan matches nothing in Epstein's island payroll; "GGLF" appears nowhere in the release.
- The licence number read on air — a few digits off; the licence itself is real. "Brunel founded NEXT" — contested by Brunel's own visa biography, not settled either way.
- The "17-minute transponder gap" — fails against the flight data. "Thiel was Kirk's earliest funder" — the Friesses' $10,000 came first.
- About 794 other "Kirk" documents are other Kirks; "KIRK Associates" is an OCR misread of HBRK, Kahn's firm; Erika Kellerhals is a Virgin Islands lawyer; "Natalie Barak" is a bank officer; "gtec" is an EEG maker; Karl M. Frantz is not family; the "Bernard Marcus" in Peter Attia's emails is a clinician; "I began relations between this new China and Israel" is pasted Shimon Peres text; "TSG / Patrick" is a water-plant contractor. Of about 700 names around Kirk searched, none returned "Erika Kirk" or "Frantzve."
Leave these out and nothing above can be dismissed with them.

Sources: EFTA01273198 · EFTA01273181 · EFTA01379801 · EFTA01282297 · EFTA01975835 · EFTA01613772 · EFTA00021386 · EFTA02380771 · EFTA02794377 p18 · EFTA01623281 · EFTA01296172 p1 · EFTA01294516 p30 · EFTA00850125 · local audit Q1 (529 pages / 463 IDs)

— THE RECORDS THAT WOULD FINISH HIS LIST —
Each is a named record held by a named custodian. Ask for them.
1. Metro Emergency Communications' Carbyne session logs for 10 September 2025, including live-location and live-video sessions from the UVU campus.
2. The 2004 Orem subscriber on Epstein's phone, and his Salt Lake, Park City and Sundance counterparties that week.
3. The MCC SHU inmate list of 9–10 August 2019 attached to the FBI's June 2025 email; DVR2's original drives; the unredacted subpoena list.
4. Epstein's own grand-jury material, and the rest of the grand-jury record in the Maxwell case beyond the law-enforcement witnesses released (his line 2); the date the Acosta transcript first became public.
5. All 12–15 hours of Bannon's footage; the Bannon–Epstein texts on the iPhone 7 the SDNY holds as "not responsive."
6. Mehtab Syed's firing record.
7. Every page on Jena Masquelier, the unredacted six-page chain, and the record that ties the Groff correspondent to the ministry job.
8. American Center for Freedom's Texas filings, and who paid its $300,000.
9. The Wexner Foundation's transfer forms to Barak, and the Cleveland FBI file closed two days after the tip.
10. The 49,104 documents removed from the public release, and the identities behind the two redaction bars.
11. Whether the Carbyne warrants were exercised; what the estate did with the Valar stake.
12. The Goldsmiths counter-signature; the Israeli command-center company's name; whose iPad Cellebrite extracted; whom Buck Revell's "research" was for; who "Patrick" was; which Steve Baer.
13. Rockefeller University's trustee lists; whether the Thiel–Burns meeting, the Bergen trip and the December 2014 Skype call took place.
14. Turning Point's sealed donor schedules, and the donor-advised layer that hides who gave.
15. The FBI Vault files released without searchable text.

— HOW THIS WAS BUILT —
The DOJ's Epstein release (1,416,711 documents, about 2.9 million pages, ids beginning EFTA), the House Oversight estate production, the Maxwell court record, IRS and SEC filings, state licence and corporate records, the Senate's own logs and public reporting, each cited where it is used; every id is real and pullable. 🗣 marks who said a thing — attribution, never doubt about the person. 🔎 marks an open question. Nobody named here is accused of a crime; the patterns are the finding, and the questions are addressed to the people who can answer them. Where the government removed a page after publishing it, that is said. Corrections get dated entries, never silent edits.

— SYNTHESIS —
He asked for ten things. One he lived to see: Maxwell's interview, released 22 August 2025. The files that came out after his death answer five more in part — the bank records, the OPR transcript, the jail footage record, the floor, the 2007 admissions — and the rest of the trail runs through people he trusted, money he never saw, a family circle he married into, and a phone system in the city where he died.

The records that would finish his list exist. Someone has every one of them. The people named in this thread can end every open question in it by answering one.

— ONE QUESTION —
For anyone who has worked in 911 dispatch or public-records law: what does it take to obtain a consolidated dispatch center's platform session logs for a single day, and who has to sign?

— ONE ASK —
If this helped you see the picture, share the first post and send it to someone who will actually pull the documents. Every id above is checkable. Each record that comes out gets added here, dated, and each correction gets its own dated entry. Receipts first, conclusions last.

‼️ AI Coding Agents Leak 13,000+ Internal Screenshots From 300+ Companies on GitHub

Details: https://t.co/EGxu9ERG52

AI coding agents exposed more than 13,000 internal screenshots from over 300 organizations by publishing them in publicly accessible GitHub repositories, according to “PixelLeak” research.

The material spanned more than 900 repositories across cloud, healthcare, fintech, government, and AI, including several Fortune 500 companies.

The exposures began with a routine development workflow. Engineers asked coding agents to make interface changes, capture before-and-after images, and add them to pull requests for review. 

Agents operating through text-based command-line environments couldn't use the image-upload process available through GitHub’s browser interface, so they found another route.
